grammar.title: 1B: Future forms - present continuous, be going to, will / won't
grammar.explanation:
English has three main ways to talk about the future. Each one fits a different situation.

Use **be going to + infinitive** for plans you have already decided. For example, you are going to add cardio to your workout routine next month.

Also use **be going to** for predictions with clear evidence. If your friend looks exhausted after one interval, he is going to rest soon.

Use the **present continuous** for future arrangements you have already fixed. If you signed up for a race, say you are competing next Saturday.

Use **will / won't** for instant decisions, promises, and offers. You will fix your sprint technique, I promise.

Use **will** for predictions without strong evidence. Your strength will grow, and your agility will improve with practice.

Use **will** for future facts too, like the time a race starts. **Shall** is only used with I and we in questions, as in shall we stretch before the workout?
examples: I *am going to start* a new workout routine in October. (a plan already decided)
Look at those dark clouds. It *is going to rain* during the race. (prediction with evidence)
We *are competing* in the city tournament next month. (a fixed arrangement)
He *is meeting* his coach to practice sprint starts at ten tomorrow. (a future arrangement)
A: I can't finish this set. B: Don't worry, I *will help* you. (an offer)
I *won't forget* to stretch after my workout. (a promise)
I think your cardio *will feel* easier after a month of training. (a prediction)
The final *will start* at nine o'clock. (a future fact)
*Shall we try* an interval session on Friday? (a suggestion)
Her strength *will improve* if she trains regularly. (a prediction)

practice.q: When do you use 'be going to' instead of 'will'?
practice.a: Use 'be going to' for plans you already decided and for predictions with clear evidence. Use 'will' for instant decisions, promises, and offers.

practice.q: Choose the correct form: 'I (am seeing / will see) my coach tomorrow. We booked the session yesterday.'
practice.a: 'I am seeing my coach tomorrow' — it is a fixed arrangement, so use the present continuous.
